messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Spatially varying coefficient model - fail to factorize Q
parts:
the issue is a numerical singular (precision) matrix. please check that
the covariates x1, x2, ... are properly scaled

you may try the most recent testing version (which require R-4.1), and
add

inla(..., inla.mode="experimental")

this should use less RAM and be more suited to this type of model.

it might give you some errors in the options (as not all options are
allowed), but just remove those it complains about and use default

if this is still an issue, please send me code & data to rerun here to
help@...

thx
H

Many thanks for the prompt reply!

How do I properly scale the covariates in this case? Is this example as given by Chapter 6 Advanced Features | Bayesian inference with INLA (bitbucket.io)   a reasonable way?

control.predictor = list(A = A))

If not, how should I rescale my covariates? 

Many thanks in advance.

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Spatially varying coefficient model - fail to factorize Q
parts:
if a covariate take all possible values, then

x <- scale(x)

might do.

if 'x' is age, f.ex, then you might use

x <- x / 100
